magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is very aligned with Catholic teaching: AI can assist in healthcare, but it should not replace the human relationship with the patient, and being present with the dying person has a value that is not reducible to diagnostics or treatment. The expression "people will want" a human chaplain is best understood as an expectation, rather than as the sole foundation of the argument: the need also stems from the dignity of the person and the Christian call to closeness and hope.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching emphasizes that the use of AI that replaces the relationship between patient and healthcare worker can intensify loneliness and neglect human solidarity. In care for the dying, remaining beside the patient, consoling them, and being present to them can bear witness to their unique worth and hope; this does not mean that AI does not have a useful auxiliary role, but rather that it cannot take over personal responsibility and the human relationship.

sections.subtitle_en: The Last Human Role: From Hospice to "Alien" and "Heat"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Louis Kim speaks about working in hospice and the question of the last human role in healthcare
sections.content_en:
Kim then shares the topic that is personally closest to him. He left the corporate world of big tech in order to work in **hospice and palliative care**. He is preoccupied with the question: if AI becomes better at diagnostics and if almost everything in healthcare can be done better with AI, **what is the last human role?** For ontological and theological reasons, he says, you might want a human chaplain, even though a human is grumpier and less present than a robot chaplain that is perfectly attentive. He calls that a very good Catholic problem.

Sanders recalls the first film **"Alien"**. While the monster is on the ship, the captain asks the computer what their chances of survival are, and the machine replies that they have none. That message, cold like the inscription "abandon all hope", appears on the screen and the character merely reads it. Sanders imagines how the same news would feel if spoken by a human who looks you in the eye and shares your fate. That is how he thinks about hospice as well. He hopes that doctors use AI, because diagnostics are better with it. But he does not want to lie in bed while the tablet next to him rings with the news that his chances have dropped from ten to zero. He would like a human to be told: you must deliver this news.

Kim explains that this is precisely why he is drawn to **literature and film**: they can convey human compassion in situations where it makes no logic. One of his favorite film scenes is the ending of the film **"Heat"**. Pacino's character shoots De Niro's bank robber at the airport. As De Niro is dying, he reaches out his hand, and Pacino takes it, in complete silence, even though they were mortal enemies. That is, Kim says, a completely illogical and deeply human act. How do you program an algorithm or a robot to do that? That, he concludes, is a **mystery**.

sections.subtitle: Što je katolički AI? Četiri odgovora u jednoj rečenici
sections.screenshot_description: Sudionici panela redom daju jednorečenične definicije katoličkog AI-ja
sections.content:
Za kraj Louis Kim traži od svakog sudionika da u jednoj rečenici odgovori **što je katolički AI**.

- **Matthew Harvey Sanders** kaže da je pojam tek potrebno definirati. U njegovoj tvrtki katolički AI shvaćaju kao onaj koji i u odgovorima i u vlastitom unutarnjem razmatranju uvijek uzima u obzir **Učiteljstvo** i čini sve što može da bude što vjerniji.
- **Taylor Black** katolički AI opisuje kao **granicu koja se ne može dosegnuti**, a koja pomaže razumjeti što znači biti ljudska osoba u katoličkoj antropologiji.
- **Vincent Higgins** naglašava da je katolički AI **ljudski procvat i uzdizanje osobe**. Ako AI koristimo ispravno, unutar katoličke vjere, bit ćemo bolji ljudi i procvast ćemo u svijetu.
- **Louis Kim** zaključuje da je **ljudsko dostojanstvo** u srži pristupa životu općenito, a tehnologija je **pojačalo i naših najboljih i naših najgorih strana**. Katolička je tradicija, kaže, dovoljno široka da o tome promišlja.

Kim zahvaljuje sugovornicima i zatvara epizodu podcasta The Catholic Futurist.

magisterium.assessment: Tri ponuđena naglaska — vjernost Učiteljstvu, katolička antropologija te služenje ljudskom dostojanstvu i procvatu — dobro odgovaraju katoličkim mjerilima za razvoj i uporabu AI-ja. Ipak, formulacija da AI u „unutarnjem razmatranju” uzima u obzir Učiteljstvo može pogrešno sugerirati savjest ili razumijevanje; prikladnije ju je shvatiti kao svojstvo sustava koji se oblikuje i provjerava katoličkim normama, a ne kao stvarno moralno prosuđivanje AI-ja.
concerns: Izraz „unutarnje razmatranje” antropomorfizira AI, osim ako je jasno mišljen samo kao tehnički opis obrade informacija: AI nema ljudsku moralnu savjest ni odgovornost.
Nastojanje da odgovori budu vjerni Učiteljstvu ne jamči da će svaki odgovor točno prenijeti nauk; potrebni su ljudski nadzor i odgovornost.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička procjena AI-ja polazi od toga da se tehnologija treba usmjeravati služenju ljudskoj osobi i općem dobru, a ne od tvrdnje da je AI osoba ili nositelj vjere. „Katolički AI” zato je najpreciznije opisati kao sustav čiji su razvoj, uporaba i izlazi prosuđivani prema katoličkom nauku, ljudskom dostojanstvu i dobru zajednice, uz priznanje da sustav sam ne razumije moralno značenje svojih odgovora niti snosi odgovornost za njih.

magisterium.assessment_en: The three proposed emphases — fidelity to the Magisterium, Catholic anthropology, and service to human dignity and flourishing — correspond well to Catholic criteria for the development and use of AI. However, the formulation that AI takes the Magisterium into account in its "internal consideration" may erroneously suggest conscience or understanding; it is more appropriately understood as a property of a system that is shaped and verified by Catholic norms, rather than as actual moral judgment by the AI.
magisterium.enrichment_en: A Catholic assessment of AI proceeds from the premise that technology must be directed toward the service of the human person and the common good, not from the claim that AI is a person or a bearer of faith. "Catholic AI" is therefore most precisely described as a system whose development, use, and outputs are judged according to Catholic teaching, human dignity, and the good of the community, while acknowledging that the system itself does not understand the moral meaning of its answers nor bear responsibility for them.
concerns_en: The phrase "internal consideration" anthropomorphizes AI, unless it is clearly meant only as a technical description of information processing: AI does not possess human moral conscience or responsibility.
The effort to ensure that answers are faithful to the Magisterium does not guarantee that every answer will accurately convey teaching; human oversight and responsibility are required.

sections.subtitle_en: What is Catholic AI? Four answers in one sentence
sections.screenshot_description_en: Panel participants take turns giving one-sentence definitions of Catholic AI
sections.content_en:
To conclude, Louis Kim asks each participant to answer in one sentence **what Catholic AI is**.

- **Matthew Harvey Sanders** says that the term has yet to be defined. In his company, they understand Catholic AI as one that, both in its answers and in its own internal consideration, always takes into account the **Magisterium** and does everything it can to be as faithful as possible.
- **Taylor Black** describes Catholic AI as an **unreachable boundary** that helps one understand what it means to be a human person in Catholic anthropology.
- **Vincent Higgins** emphasizes that Catholic AI is **human flourishing and the elevation of the person**. If we use AI correctly, within the Catholic faith, we will be better people and we will flourish in the world.
- **Louis Kim** concludes that **human dignity** is at the core of an approach to life in general, and technology is an **amplifier of both our best and our worst sides**. The Catholic tradition, he says, is broad enough to reflect on this.

Kim thanks the interlocutors and closes the episode of The Catholic Futurist podcast.
